questions.stem: A family meeting is being held to discuss the care options for a 75-year-old woman with terminal lung cancer. The two caregivers are as follows: • Kanda, who has been caring for her at the bedside for the past year, does not want chemotherapy and wishes for her mother to have a peaceful passing. • Kedkaew, who handles the financial matters, wants the patient to receive full-option treatment. What should the doctor do?

choices.A: Follow Kedkaew’s request as the decision-maker
choices.B: Follow Kanda’s request, focusing on a holistic approach
choices.C: Ask the family to nominate the primary caregiver and follow that decision
choices.D: Use the law to make a decision
choices.E: Ask both caregivers to review and select the option that best aligns with the patient's wishes
